learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected A and locked it in.
observations.exploration: One step on stream A A A B B C C made candidate A and counter one. Run stream one finished candidate C and counter one. Count again showed C two of seven, not majority, while A had three. Stream two A A B A C A A finished A, counter three, with five of seven confirmed. Reset returned original stream at zero processed while preserving both completed traces.
observations.reveal: Corrected to C, explained cancellation of unlike pairs, no guarantee without a more-than-half item, and true majority survival. Second pass verifies whether a majority exists.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Letter cards use distinct fills and outlines; per-position candidate-counter traces visible after run. Reveal after reset clearly retained historical counts and displayed current zero state, with readable explanation.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Explicit candidate-counter rules support exact process prediction.
prediction.evidence: A versus B versus C on seven-item stream.

interaction.reason: Step, complete run, verification, alternate stream and reset expose guarantee boundary.
interaction.evidence: C survives without plurality; A survives with five-of-seven majority.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains cancellation and necessity of verification.
payoff.evidence: More-than-half copies cannot all be cancelled.

clarity.reason: Candidate, counter and verified frequency remain distinct.
clarity.evidence: Counter one does not equal C frequency two; second pass reports actual count.

transfer.reason: General majority condition explained with second stream but no new application.
transfer.evidence: Same stream algorithm on two sequences.

accessibility.evidence: Text stream, candidate and verified counts available; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Most frequent item can lose candidate cancellation.
surprise.evidence: A three occurrences versus C two, final C.

visualExplanation.evidence: A counter rises then drops before C selected.

playfulness.reason: Step and alternate stream support algorithm exploration.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies what a low-memory majority detector guarantees.

depth.reason: Separates plurality, majority, candidate and proof condition.
depth.evidence: True majority cannot be fully cancelled.

complexity.reason: Simple letter stream requires an invariant and guarantee reasoning.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Track a cancellation counter distinct from frequency and understand conditional majority guarantee.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Five contextual buttons and retained traces.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Majority-candidate algorithm and second verification pass.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Letters, counters, plus/minus one and counts out of seven.

whyCool: A cancellation survivor is a candidate, not proof of being most common.
caveat: Two fixed streams demonstrate the boundary; no fresh arbitrary stream or new application was tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
